Where OneOps sits

Applications, enterprise users, and autonomous agents send requests through a shared operational layer. Amazon Bedrock provides foundation model inference. OneOps brings access policy, routing, observability, and cost allocation together around each invocation.

For platform teams, that means applications can keep using standard Bedrock SDK interfaces while central teams manage the rules for permitted models, regions, and workloads.

Before model execution

Identity establishes the team or project responsible for a request. The control layer evaluates model permissions, regional boundaries, and the remaining budget. An application or agent that reaches its configured ceiling follows the organization’s fallback policy.

In-flight inspection applies the configured treatment for personally identifiable information, credentials, and other sensitive material. The resulting policy decision becomes part of the audit trail.

Explore security and governance

Choosing an inference path

Five levers shape how an eligible request reaches Bedrock. Model selection matches the task to the required reasoning effort. Regional routing directs traffic within approved boundaries. Prompt caching reuses common context, compression trims the payload, and batch inference groups work that can tolerate a deferred response.

Workload latency requirements and output quality determine which levers are appropriate. Compare equivalent tasks before and after a routing change to see its effect.

Explore the five savings levers

From traces to reports

Request telemetry ties token counts, response speed, policy decisions, and estimated spend to the originating workload. Engineers can investigate slow requests while security teams review guardrail events.

Finance can aggregate usage by team or project for monthly showback and chargeback. The weekly digest brings spend, savings, risk events, and active projects into a shared view for leadership.
